items.title: Google Antigravity Ships /swarm: Multi-Agent Coding Orchestration Powered by Gemini 4 Carbon
items.summary: Google previewed the /swarm command inside Antigravity (desktop app and CLI) on November 10, coordinating parallel coding workers, independent diff verifiers, and a stall monitor over one shared, zero-idle-cost message board. Backed by the newly released Gemini 4 Carbon, the setup has already delivered a complete open-world 3D game and, from seven city-planning PDFs (206 engineering drawings), an interactive 3D model of ~906,000 triangles generated in a single overnight run.
items.impact: This is the 'coordination before generation' thesis made native in the IDE: the bottleneck has shifted from writing code to orchestrating, verifying, and recovering across many agents. For builders, the lesson is that a managed agent team (roles + independent review + stall detection) now beats a single stronger model. Watch the cost model — shared boards and parallel workers can quietly multiply token spend.

items.title: Cursor Launches Multiplayer Projects for Human + Agent Collaboration
items.summary: Rolled out in beta to all Cursor users on November 10, Multiplayer Projects lets engineering, design, and product teammates collaborate alongside their coding agents on one shared board. Rather than each person running a private agent, the work — and the agents — live in a single shared surface where teammates assign, review, and track changes together.
items.impact: Coding agents are moving from solo assistants to team-level, collaborative surfaces. Combined with GitHub's four-stage workflow and Antigravity's /swarm, the industry is converging on one pattern: agents need defined roles, shared context, and explicit authority to be useful at team scale. The competitive axis is shifting from 'best model' to 'best multiplayer operating system for agents.'

items.title: OpenAI's dot Adds Multi-Computer Orchestration Across Cloud Devboxes, GPUs, and Laptops
items.summary: OpenAI updated dot (formerly a local coding agent) so developers can manage tasks spanning remote Linux servers, GPU instances, and secondary laptops from a single local workspace. The same task can fan out across heterogeneous compute — a cloud devbox for builds, a GPU box for heavy jobs, a laptop for local checks — without leaving one command surface.
items.impact: The line between 'local' and 'cloud' development is dissolving. As agents take on longer, heavier jobs, the ability to schedule work across machines becomes core infrastructure, not a nice-to-have. Teams should plan for agent identities and permissions that follow workloads across hosts, not just within one machine.

items.title: NVIDIA Unveils GR00T 2: A 2B-Parameter 'World Action Model' That Runs On-Robot
items.summary: Presented at the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) on November 9, GR00T 2 is a 2-billion-parameter world action model built on Cosmos. It predicts future video frames and robot actions in one diffusion pass. NVIDIA reports 71% average success across 50 tasks from a single demonstration per task, rising to 95% with five demos (under three minutes of robot data each, then a ~30-minute RTX 5090 fine-tune). The lighter GR00T 2 Turbo runs onboard a Unitree G1 on a Jetson AGX Thor at 124 ms per prediction; open weights and the cross-embodiment training recipe arrive in December. Foxconn, Siemens, and MicroAGI are already testing it in factories and cable-handling work.
items.impact: GR00T 2 marks two shifts at once: robot 'brains' moving to edge/onboard real-time inference, and skills transferring across robot bodies from human video — sharply lowering the data and fine-tuning barrier. It reinforces that the future is a fast 'System 1' skill model steered by a reasoning 'System 2,' and that sim-to-real plus cross-embodiment transfer — not just bigger models — is where embodied intelligence compounds.

items.title: Humanoid Mass Production Crosses From Demos to Volume: AgiBot 20k, Figure BotQ, Tesla's Fremont Line
items.summary: The November 2026 deployment tracker shows the sector scaling hard: AgiBot has produced 20,000 units across all series; Figure's BotQ has built 1,000+ Figure 03 units at a rate of one robot per hour; Tesla disclosed Optimus assembly on its Fremont high-volume line (Musk: ~20,000/week is a year-plus away, external customers possibly by end of 2027); and Unitree targets 10,000–20,000+ units in 2026. Asia-Pacific accounts for roughly 80–90% of deployments, with Boston Dynamics' Atlas, Agility's Digit, and 1X's NEO advancing in the US and Europe.
items.impact: Embodied intelligence is crossing the prototype-to-volume threshold that separates hype from industry. The signal to watch is no longer 'how many shipped' but 'how many run continuously and pay back' — reliability, payload, and stable uptime are the real constraints. China's manufacturing base is setting the production tempo, framing 2027 as the first year of commercial external deliveries.
